chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Najiya, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one in Ihram whose ears are hit by the wind, so he fears that he would fall sick. Is it correct for him that he closes his ears with the cotton? He said: Yes, there is no problem with that when he fears that, or else, so no.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram plug their ears with cotton to prevent illness from wind?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-darar* (avoiding harm) within the strictures of Ihram, allowing a temporary concession for health preservation. It highlights the scholarly distinction between mere precaution and genuine fear of illness, a nuance often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of breaking Ihram restrictions for medical necessity. The ruling underscores the balance between ritual purity and physical well-being, a core theme in Usuli jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Najiya, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Marwan Bin Muslim, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam whose ears are hit by the wind, so he fears that he would fall sick. Is it correct for him that he closes his ears with the cotton?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, there is no problem with that when he fears that, or else, so no’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Najiyah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Marwan ibn Muslim from who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram, his ears are affected by winds and is afraid of illness; if he can place cotton in his ears. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if he is afraid of illness, otherwise, it is not permissible.’”
